assumptions: Requirement IDs were supplied without individual definitions; coverage descriptions map the prompt requirements in their presented order.
The supplied local TypeScript API and Chrome installation are available; build.mjs documents the environment-specific compiler path.
decisions: Used a monotonically increasing request identifier and guarded both Promise fulfillment and rejection because cancellation is unsupported.
Kept Search enabled while pending and cleared prior outcomes when a new query starts.
Retry stores the failed submitted query independently of input edits and focuses the input before hiding Retry.
Used native form behavior, polite live status, error alert, busy result container, visible focus outlines and reduced-motion support.
Used an editorial field-library style with warm paper, forest green and wrapped serif guide titles.

checks.evidence: evidence/moss.png and evidence/mobile-accessibility.png viewed; long title wraps and controls fit at 320px
No screen reader execution; semantic DOM observations only

limitations: Assistive-technology announcements have semantic DOM checks but were not heard with a screen reader.
Keyboard and desktop Chrome automation performed; additional browsers and real touch hardware were not tested.
Compiler path is specific to the supplied environment.
The first fixture read and first test-script write failed due to path assumptions; retained in evidence/tooling-errors.log and corrected before successful checks.
The patch tool took roughly two minutes; all recorded elapsed time includes that delay. Tool-call target counting waits may be exceeded; no usage or monetary telemetry is available.
Final JSON inspection found a PowerShell array wrapper around browser checks; normalized to the required flat checks array before delivery.
